subject: Chemistry
title: Nucleophilic Substitution Explained: KCN vs AgCN, Ambident Nucleophiles
summary: A nucleophile (an electron-rich species) replaces the halogen of a haloalkane: Nu⁻ + R–X → R–Nu + X⁻. In this lesson: why the δ+ carbon is attacked, the leaving group, the general mechanism with two curved arrows, SN2 vs SN1 named, the nucleophile decides the product (alcohol, ether, amine, nitrile, ester), and ambident nucleophiles: KCN vs AgCN, KNO2 vs AgNO2. Two questions solved, including a JEE Main 2024 PYQ.

notes.title: Nucleophilic Substitution Explained
notes.blurb: why it happens, the general mechanism, the nucleophile decides the product, ambident nucleophiles

keyPoints: **The reaction**: The **δ+ carbon** is the reactive centre. X⁻ is the **leaving group**.
**Two arrows**: **SN2**: one step. **SN1**: two steps, via a **carbocation**.
**Nucleophile → product**: Change the **nucleophile**, change the product. Leaving group: **R–I fastest**, R–F slowest.
**Ambident**: KCN ionic: attack via **C**. AgCN covalent: attack via **N**.

blocks.p: The C–X bond is polar: X is more electronegative, so the carbon carries a partial positive charge (δ+). This δ+ carbon is the **reactive centre** that the nucleophile attacks. The halogen leaves with the bonding pair as X⁻: the **leaving group**.
Two curved arrows: (1) a lone pair of the nucleophile → the δ+ carbon (new C–Nu bond); (2) the C–X bond pair → X (X⁻ leaves). Example: CH₃CH₂Br + OH⁻ (aqueous KOH) → CH₃CH₂OH + Br⁻.
The substitution follows one of two paths: **SN2** (one step) or **SN1** (two steps, through a carbocation).
Leaving-group ability follows the C–X bond strength: **R–I > R–Br > R–Cl > R–F** in reactivity.

Nucleophiles with two attacking sites: CN⁻ (C or N) and NO₂⁻ (O or N). **KCN** is ionic, so free CN⁻ attacks through carbon (C–C bond is more stable): alkyl cyanide. **AgCN** is mainly covalent; carbon is bonded to silver, so the lone pair on nitrogen attacks: isocyanide. Similarly KNO₂ gives alkyl nitrites, AgNO₂ gives nitroalkanes.

list: ✗ The halogen-bearing carbon is δ− (it is δ+).

blocks.p: **Q1.** CH₃CH₂Br + (a) aq KOH → CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol) (b) KCN → CH₃CH₂CN (propanenitrile) (c) AgCN → CH₃CH₂NC (ethyl isocyanide).
**Q2 (JEE Main 2024, 29 Jan, Evening).** Alkyl halide → alkyl isocyanide: **AgCN**.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: Alkyl halide is converted into alkyl isocyanide by reaction with:
pyq.explain: AgCN Covalent AgCN: the N lone pair attacks → R–NC.

pyq.q: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–Br gives A with AgNO₂ and B with AgCN. A and B respectively are:
pyq.explain: AgNO₂ attacks through N → 1-nitropropane; AgCN through N → propyl isocyanide.
